text:
Chris: Heads-up — nightly perf job showed a 3x tail-latency spike on int8-packed runs after merging the linker reorder for triton. seeing a lot of 'selected_kernel=generic_gemm' in the trace :confused:
Maya: ugh. which commit? can you paste a minimal log snippet?
Chris: merged 2026-03-17T22:08:03 (linker-order-fix). here's the grep from the runtime profiler:```
[00:01:12] model=llama-3b quant=int8 seq=128 selected_kernel=generic_gemm fallback_reason=alignment_mismatch sm_arch=sm89
[00:01:12] model=llama-3b quant=int8 selected_kernel=triton_cutlass_fp8 packed=false
[00:01:12] perf_ms=120 selected_kernel=generic_gemm
```
Li: interesting that sm_arch=sm89 but kernel registry should have sm89 optimized kernels. maybe runtime is failing to match the CUTLASS registry entry after the linker change.
Sam: could be symbol collision or registration order — CUTLASS uses static registration at link time. if the object containing sm89 kernels is dropped or reordered, registration could default to generic fallback.
Frank: also saw a stray zero-scale value in calibration output for that run earlier. if quant scales are 0.0 it may trigger a path that bypasses packed kernels. not sure.
Chris: confirmed: the calibration file had one layer with scale=0.0 (weird). but the generic_gemm appears even for layers with sane scales.
Maya: can you reproduce locally with a single-run script? if so, try LD_PRELOAD with the old object ordering or run with CUTLASS_REGISTRY_VERBOSE=1 to dump registry contents.
Chris: repro script: `./scripts/profiler/run_single.sh --model llama-3b --quant int8 --seq 128 --batch 1`
Chris: output with env: `CUTLASS_REGISTRY_VERBOSE=1` shows registry entries but sm89 entries appear after generic, and the runtime log shows 'registered_kernels=[generic_gemm, triton_cutlass_int8_sm86, triton_cutlass_fp8_sm89]' — the runtime selects the first compatible entry, which now is generic.
Sam: ok that matches linker-order hypothesis. simplest workaround: add a weak alias to ensure optimized kernels register earlier, or change selection to prefer highest-throughput rank rather than first-match.
Li: changing selection algorithm might be safer long-term. first-match is fragile. we should prefer by throughput estimate then compatibility.
Frank: agree. quick mitigation: add a build flag to force keep-alive of triton_cutlass objects (`-Wl,--whole-archive`) for the CUTLASS kernel pack.
Maya: can someone try the whole-archive build locally and rerun the nightly?
Chris: doing that now — building with `bazel build //runtime:inference_bin --linkopt=-Wl,--whole-archive --linkopt=-Wl,--no-whole-archive`
dev-bot: build started for //runtime:inference_bin (id: bld-20260318-1143)
Chris: quick run after rebuild — latency back to baseline (perf_ms ~ 35). seems to confirm registration/order issue.
Sam: good. open PR for selection change + add regression test that validates registry ordering isn't relied on. also add a small unit test that fakes a zero-scale calibration and ensures kernel selection still prefers optimized kernel.
Maya: I'll own the selection-change PR. Frank, can you add the whole-archive linker flag to the CI artifacts as an interim until PR lands?
Frank: yes, I'll patch the build matrix for the dedicated-nightly job.
ops-bot: deploy pipeline alert: nightly-dedicated build will be re-run with updated linker flags at 03:00 UTC
Chris: thanks — putting a note in the PERF board and adding the logs to the incident thread. follow-ups: (1) bisect whether calibration tool produced zero scales or if data caused it, (2) implement selection-by-throughput rank, (3) CI guard to prevent accidental linker reorder.
Maya: documented. thx all :thumbsup:
Li: small note — check that this doesn't mask actual incompatibility (alignment truly incompatible). prefer selection rank but still keep strict compatibility checks.
Sam: agreed.
Chris: closing loop here. will update when PRs are up.
